does-insurance-cover-ev-battery-fire-cha.label: Illustrative chart.
does-insurance-cover-ev-battery-fire-cha.alt: Hypothetical covered repair of $10,000: insurer share $9,000 and owner deductible $1,000, assuming no other adjustments.
does-insurance-cover-ev-battery-fire-cha.caption: Hypothetical covered $10,000 repair. Illustration only: $1,000 deductible; no other adjustments.

does-insurance-cover-ev-battery-fire-inf.label: Illustrative infographic.
does-insurance-cover-ev-battery-fire-inf.alt: After an EV fire: keep the decisions separate. People first: Move away and call emergency services. Do not return to investigate the battery. Qualified handling: Let responders and trained recovery personnel decide how the EV is handled. Record the facts: Once safe, keep incident references, existing records and insurer correspondence. Read the contract: Separate vehicle damage, the failed component and damage beyond the car.
does-insurance-cover-ev-battery-fire-inf.caption: After an EV fire: keep the decisions separate.

hurricane-storm-damage-electric-car-insu.label: Illustrative chart.
hurricane-storm-damage-electric-car-insu.alt: At an assumed $45 daily rental rate, 7 days costs $315, 14 days $630 and 21 days $945. These are not policy benefits.
hurricane-storm-damage-electric-car-insu.caption: Hypothetical rental cost at $45 per day. 7 days: $315; 14 days: $630; 21 days: $945. Not a benefit limit.

hurricane-storm-damage-electric-car-insu.label: Illustrative infographic.
hurricane-storm-damage-electric-car-insu.alt: After a storm: safety before settlement. Keep your distance: Do not enter floodwater or approach an electrically unsafe vehicle. Report accurately: Describe flood, hail, falling debris or a collision without guessing the cause. Arrange assessment: Confirm a qualified destination and recovery instructions with professionals. Check each policy: Vehicle, charger and building damage can involve different contracts.
hurricane-storm-damage-electric-car-insu.caption: After a storm: safety before settlement.

what-happens-to-electric-car-after-crash.label: Illustrative chart.
what-happens-to-electric-car-after-crash.alt: Hypothetical storage at $35 per day totals $105 after 3 days, $245 after 7 days and $490 after 14 days. Payment depends on authorization and policy terms.
what-happens-to-electric-car-after-crash.caption: Hypothetical storage cost at $35 per day. 3 days: $105; 7 days: $245; 14 days: $490. Not a market rate.

what-happens-to-electric-car-after-crash.label: Illustrative infographic.
what-happens-to-electric-car-after-crash.alt: A crash claim: the owner's four checkpoints. Make people safe: Tell responders an EV is involved; do not assess high-voltage damage yourself. Confirm recovery: Ask whether the operator follows this model's manufacturer instructions. Separate decisions: Safety assessment, coverage review and repair approval are not the same decision. Check the outcome: Retain the repair documents or valuation and clarify any outstanding costs.
what-happens-to-electric-car-after-crash.caption: A crash claim: the owner's four checkpoints.

war-exclusion-car-insurance-policy-chart.label: Illustrative chart.
war-exclusion-car-insurance-policy-chart.alt: For an entirely hypothetical $10,000 loss, assuming full coverage subject only to a $1,000 deductible gives $9,000; assuming the entire loss is validly excluded gives $0. This does not classify any real event or policy.
war-exclusion-car-insurance-policy-chart.caption: Two hypothetical outcomes for a $10,000 loss. Assumptions: covered less $1,000 deductible, or fully excluded.

war-exclusion-car-insurance-policy-infog.label: Illustrative infographic.
war-exclusion-car-insurance-policy-infog.alt: When an exclusion is raised: ask for specifics. Get the wording: Obtain the policy, schedule and applicable endorsements. Separate cause and damage: A fire or explosion label alone does not determine the legal cause. Request the reasoning: Ask which facts and exact clause support the insurer's written decision. Use local review routes: Follow the complaint process and seek qualified advice where appropriate.
war-exclusion-car-insurance-policy-infog.caption: When an exclusion is raised: ask for specifics.

electric-vehicle-auto-body-repair-chart.label: Illustrative chart.
electric-vehicle-auto-body-repair-chart.alt: Hypothetical $4,700 body repair: parts $2,000, labor $1,500, paint and materials $900 and documented checks $300. These are illustrative amounts, not a quote or required repair procedure.
electric-vehicle-auto-body-repair-chart.caption: Hypothetical $4,700 body-repair estimate. Illustration: $2,000 + $1,500 + $900 + $300; not a quote.

electric-vehicle-auto-body-repair-infogr.label: Illustrative infographic.
electric-vehicle-auto-body-repair-infogr.alt: Read a body-repair estimate in four passes. Damage and method: Ask what is cosmetic, structural or related to vehicle systems. Parts and labor: Check the itemised proposed work rather than comparing totals alone. Specialist operations: Ask which model-specific procedures and post-repair checks apply. Authorization and handover: Separate insurer approval from your consent and keep the final records.
electric-vehicle-auto-body-repair-infogr.caption: Read a body-repair estimate in four passes.

how-much-does-it-cost-to-charge-electric.label: Illustrative chart.
how-much-does-it-cost-to-charge-electric.alt: At the article's assumed 30 kWh per 100 miles, energy costs are $4.50 at $0.15 per kWh, $7.50 at $0.25 and $15 at $0.50, excluding other fees.
how-much-does-it-cost-to-charge-electric.caption: Energy cost per 100 miles at 30 kWh/100 miles. Hypothetical rates; excludes session fees and other charges.

how-much-does-it-cost-to-charge-electric.label: Illustrative infographic.
how-much-does-it-cost-to-charge-electric.alt: Build a charging budget from your own inputs. Read the energy unit: kW is power; kWh is energy. Find the energy you are actually buying. Use your rate: Check home tariffs or the public charger's actual pricing and fees. Multiply carefully: Energy bought times price per kWh gives the energy part of the bill. Add what is missing: Check losses, subscriptions, session fees and the mix of charging locations.
how-much-does-it-cost-to-charge-electric.caption: Build a charging budget from your own inputs.

ev-insurance-chart.label: Illustrative chart.
ev-insurance-chart.alt: At the article's hypothetical $180 annual premium saving, cumulative savings are $180 over 1 year, $540 over 3, $900 over 5 and $1,080 over 6, assuming unchanged premiums and no claims. The example increases the deductible by $1,000.
ev-insurance-chart.caption: Article example: $180 saved per claim-free year. 1, 3, 5 and 6 years: $180, $540, $900 and $1,080. No forecast.

ev-insurance-infographic.label: Illustrative infographic.
ev-insurance-infographic.alt: Build EV protection around the actual questions. Meet local requirements: Identify the jurisdiction and any lender conditions. Protect the vehicle: Read collision, comprehensive and battery-related wording. Check practical benefits: Review recovery, temporary transport and charging equipment separately. Compare equal cover: Match limits and deductibles, then read the final price and exclusions.
ev-insurance-infographic.caption: Build EV protection around the actual questions.

electric-car-insurance-cost-chart.label: Illustrative chart.
electric-car-insurance-cost-chart.alt: In the article's hypothetical covered $6,000 collision example, annual premium plus deductible is $3,300 for Quote A and $2,540 for Quote B, before other adjustments, costs or benefits.
electric-car-insurance-cost-chart.caption: Article example: premium plus collision deductible. Covered $6,000 repair; A: $1,800+$1,500; B: $2,040+$500.

electric-car-insurance-cost-infographic.label: Illustrative infographic.
electric-car-insurance-cost-infographic.alt: Make two insurance prices genuinely comparable. Use the same vehicle: Match drivers, address, mileage, use and exact trim. Match the protection: Record limits, collision, comprehensive and optional benefits. Read the trade-offs: A deductible or rental benefit difference changes the product. Compare final totals: Use the same coverage period and include applicable payment fees.
electric-car-insurance-cost-infographic.caption: Make two insurance prices genuinely comparable.

tesla-insurance-coverage-cost-comparison.label: Illustrative chart.
tesla-insurance-coverage-cost-comparison.alt: Hypothetical equal $1,000 annual premiums: a no-fee payment plan totals $1,000; a plan adding $8 monthly fees totals $1,096. These are not Tesla or another insurer's quoted prices.
tesla-insurance-coverage-cost-comparison.caption: Hypothetical $1,000 premium under two payment plans. A: no fees; B: $8 per month in fees. Not a Tesla quote.

tesla-insurance-coverage-cost-comparison.label: Illustrative infographic.
tesla-insurance-coverage-cost-comparison.alt: Compare the policy, not only the Tesla name. Confirm availability: Check which state-specific product and terms are actually offered. Read driving-data terms: Safety Score is not used for California premiums, per Tesla's cited guidance. Match the cover: Compare limits, deductibles, repair terms and total-loss settlement basis. Switch without a gap: Confirm new cover is in force before canceling an existing policy.
tesla-insurance-coverage-cost-comparison.caption: Compare the policy, not only the Tesla name.

gap-insurance-electric-car-chart.label: Illustrative chart.
gap-insurance-electric-car-chart.alt: The article's hypothetical $34,000 loan balance consists of a $29,000 net auto payment and a $5,000 remaining difference. The GAP contract, not this chart, determines any eligible benefit.
gap-insurance-electric-car-chart.caption: Article example: $34,000 outstanding balance. $30,000 value minus $1,000 deductible = $29,000 net payment.

gap-insurance-electric-car-infographic.label: Illustrative infographic.
gap-insurance-electric-car-infographic.alt: Before buying GAP: work through four checks. Get the two figures: Use the current lender balance and a relevant vehicle value estimate. Read the trigger: Check theft or total-loss requirements and required auto insurance. Calculate eligible amounts: Ask how deductibles, financed add-ons, exclusions and caps are treated. Check the exit terms: Read cancellation, refund, sale and refinance provisions before signing.
gap-insurance-electric-car-infographic.caption: Before buying GAP: work through four checks.
